name: She'kspere (Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs)
notes: The 1999 "jittery post-Timbaland R&B" sound — plucked acoustic and harpsichord patches over stop-start programming, 1998–2002. The research gives "**64–93**: 'Bills, Bills, Bills' 64 half-time, 'No Scrubs' 93 straight"; the straight half is encoded, and because the half-time subset is the single 64 point the straight complement is 65–93, with the mode at the sourced 93. The entry's Keys line also names "Bug a Boo" at 104, above the band its own Lane line declares; the declared band governs here, so that cut is not folded in. The drum claim is stated as *the* defining parameter and the model is built to it: "the defining parameter is **gapping** — hyper-finessed 'insectile stop-start surfaces': kick and snare land on unexpected 16ths, hats appear in one-bar bursts and then vanish, and silence is used as a rhythmic hit. Everything is quantised hard, dry, and small-sounding by design." So `syncopation` is 0.82 with a 0.34 `beatSkipProb` — the highest skip rate in this section — the hat is non-continuous at 0.52 fill density, `quantizeStrength` is 0.98 with `offGridMs` 0, `velocityVar` is 0.1, and the `velocityTiers` are deliberately low (96–110 accent over a 64–78 main), which is what "small-sounding by design" means when the only control is dynamics. Harmony is "a two-bar plucked figure over a 2-chord minor vamp" on "a **Kurzweil acoustic-guitar** patch" or harpsichord-synths, so `maxChords` is 2 with a triad-leaning spread and a guitar timbre hint. "Minor-mode with quirky, non-diatonic melodic turns" is why `halfStepDissonance` is 0.26 and `chordToneBias` drops to 0.66 — the pluck does not spell the chord. "He composes by beatboxing the rhythm first, then builds the plucked figure over it" is the riff-dominant contour and `twoBarCellRepeat`. The bass is "a thin, dry, short-decay sub that leaves the mid-range clear for the plucked lead; no slides or sustain" — `mirror_kick`, `glideProb` 0, a single-degree cell, and no `bass808` block. ⚠ Every velocity and density number is INFERRED. ⚠ `session.keys` is part-sourced: the entry names `Abm`, `Bm`, `F#`, and the remaining value `Fm`, together with all 4 weights, are INFERRED rather than read from the entry. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "playing a two-bar plucked figure over a 2-chord minor vamp", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so weighting `vamp` at the top rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The chord motion the entry states is now carried by `1_per_bar` (the pair over a 2-bar cell) and `2_bars_per_chord` (the pair over a 4-bar cell), with `vamp` kept as the minority for the held reading. A 2-chord vamp under a **two-bar** figure is one chord a bar, hence `1_per_bar` at the top weight. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate.
